rv.q: Jesse Tyler Ferguson impresses as Truman Capote in this slender drama from Allen

In New York, Ferguson’s take on Tru got solid reviews that were slightly tempered by the extreme ticket price: it was staged in the spectacular library of Gilded Age mansion House of the Redeemer. Here it’ll just be at the good ol’ Menier: still intimate, but at a more reasonable price.
If you miss the chance to see Tyler Ferguson in this role, you are missing a career defining performance.
Ashford has chosen to make this element of the script explicit, to great effect, even if it doesn't quite overcome the shortcomings of the script.
Though it isn't perfect by a long shot, what Tru gets right puts it among the best I have seen this year.
Staging TRU in such intimate fashion gives the audience a front-row seat into a world of royal scandal and power couple infidelities that plays on much that still feels relevant to today's world.

cn.t: Ferguson delivers a captivating performance as Truman Capote in this intimate one-man show, drawn entirely from the writer's own words, that critics praise for its compelling portrayal of the author in crisis.

dr.inst: Available via TodayTix app only. Until 14 November 2026.
